purpose: Keep the job-application ecosystem current from one evidence-bound coordination source while separating the admitted public portfolio subset from the authenticated owned-estate intelligence substrate, without copying child repository source, creating competing inventories, or granting Helix project-direction authority over peer repositories.

truth_model.child_source_authority: Each child repository remains authoritative for its own code, README, tests, releases, repository-native receipts, and factual runtime state.
truth_model.portfolio_authority: NO_PROJECT_DIRECTION_AUTHORITY: Helix coordinates admitted-portfolio classification, authenticated-estate compiler policy, evidence-bound lineage and support assertions, capability projection, company alignment, second-depth evidence progression, and public/private projection boundaries. These coordination functions do not grant Helix authority to redefine Operator intent, peer-repository purpose, architecture targets, or factual source state.
truth_model.projection_rule: Downstream systems consume links, public-safe policies, and generated snapshots only. They do not become independent sources of truth or project-direction authority, and public consumers never require the authenticated census or private estate identities.

sources.role: Admitted 67-repository public-portfolio boundary; not the full authenticated owned estate and not authority over child-repository purpose
Projection, provenance, and no-copy policy for the admitted portfolio
SHA-bound repository observations and evidence state
Evidence-backed flagship hierarchy, public boundary, and next gates
Company-track index and dossier shard contract
Company-specific evidence progression, stage prerequisites, blockers, next gates, and public claim ceilings
Fail-closed repository-quality scoring policy that evaluates evidence without acquiring project-direction authority
Authenticated owned-estate compiler policy for namespace isolation, lineage collapse, evidence-supported system groupings, capability donors, company projection, and public-safe output
Public-safe role-capability rules, audience proof-surface caps, support ancestry semantics, and truth boundaries
Evidence-bound namespace, lineage, and support assertions for private estate compilation; unsupported relations remain unpromoted
Dated external company operating-pressure snapshot with official-source observations separated from GlacierEQ inference and explicit refresh requirements

projections.boundary: The public portal may consume only public-safe estate policy and external-intelligence metadata. It must not consume estate_facts, the authenticated census, private repository identities, legal-private records, or raw owned-estate cardinality.
Résumé projections may use public-safe role and company intelligence policy but may not consume estate_facts, authenticated census records, or private repository identities.
Private estate facts may inform internal compilation, but generated company packets must pass the estate public-safe projection boundary before publication.
Machine-public surfaces inherit the same hard exclusion of authenticated census rows, estate_facts, legal-private identities, and raw owned-estate cardinality.
Cloud projections may hold private operational metadata, including evidence-bound estate assertions, but public projections must consume only public-safe fields.

event_triggers: company second-depth stage or evidence change
estate compiler or projection policy change
evidence-bound estate namespace lineage or support assertion change
required_sequence: validate all required control-plane source files
validate company second-depth stages, prerequisites, blockers, and claim ceilings
verify every HELIX_ADMITTED repository maps to admitted inventory
verify every admitted inventory child maps to at least one tracked company or GlacierEQ Core evidence surface
when authenticated estate access is available, census the full owned estate without committing private census rows
apply evidence-bound namespace lineage and support assertions fail closed
compile evidence-supported systems, capability donors, company projections, and experiment state
compile public-safe and private projections separately
update_contract.consumer_behavior: Consumers must reject missing required sources, schema drift, duplicate identities, private-record leakage, unsupported claims, stale source receipts, second-depth stage claims that lack their declared prerequisites, and any public surface that exposes authenticated-estate identities or cardinality. Consumers must not infer project-direction authority from Helix coordination state.

invariants: The admitted inventory root plus workspace repository count equals its total_repositories field.
The 67-repository inventory is the admitted public-portfolio subset, not the full authenticated owned estate.
Authenticated owned-estate cardinality and private repository identities remain runtime-private and absent from downstream public bundles.
Workspace repository identities in the admitted inventory are unique.
Every HELIX_ADMITTED dossier repository exists in the admitted inventory.
Every admitted inventory child appears in at least one tracked company or GlacierEQ Core evidence surface.
Every required company track resolves to a fail-closed second-depth evidence state; missing overrides never imply completion.
Second-depth stages are monotonic and public claim ceilings may not exceed the strongest satisfied stage prerequisites.
Evidence-bound dependency and reference support never collapses lineage or counts as an independent accomplishment.
Legal-private estate material is hard-isolated from company, recruiter, resume, and machine-public projections.
L0, QUARANTINED, EXCLUDED, and private-only records never enter public recruiter projections.
Company naming never implies affiliation, endorsement, employment, proprietary access, contract relationship, clearance, or production deployment.
Repository ownership does not by itself establish authorship, originality, security, runtime success, recruiter readiness, or project-direction authority.
Downstream projections may change presentation but may not change factual IDs, evidence states, second-depth stages, claim ceilings, test counts, blockers, or source boundaries.
Helix coordination, evidence, projection, verification, ranking, and receipt functions never grant project-direction authority over the Operator or peer repositories.
